Here’s a 1-week deload that keeps the same exercise menu your client has been using, but meaningfully reduces both volume and intensity to promote recovery while maintaining movement patterns and skill. Assumes a 4-day split similar to common hypertrophy templates (adjust exercise names to match exactly what he’s been running). If he’s on a different split, keep the structure and apply the same set/rep/intensity rules.

Global deload rules
- Intensity: RPE 6–7 on all lifts (2–4 reps in reserve). No grinders, no sets to failure.
- Volume: Reduce hard sets per exercise by ~50–60% versus his hypertrophy block. Typically 2–3 work sets per main lift and 1–2 for accessories.
- Load guidance: Start ~70–75% of the loads he used for RPE 8.5, adjust to stay within RPE 6–7.
- Tempo: Controlled eccentrics (2–3 seconds) to maintain technique; normal concentrics; pause 1s at weak points as desired.
- Rest: 2–3 min on compounds, 60–90s on accessories.
- Conditioning: Light zone 2 (optional) 15–20 min, 1–2x, separate from lifting or after sessions.
- Mobility: 5–8 min targeted mobility and breathing at session end.

Week 5 Deload (4 sessions)

Day 1: Lower 1 (Squat focus)
- Back Squat: 3 sets x 3–5 reps @ RPE 6–7
- Romanian Deadlift: 2 x 5–6 @ RPE 6–7
- Walking Lunge or Split Squat: 2 x 6–8/side @ RPE 6
- Leg Curl (machine or cable): 2 x 8–10 @ RPE 6–7
- Calf Raise: 2 x 10–12 @ RPE 6
- Core: Dead bug or Pallof press: 2 x 10–12 controlled

Day 2: Upper 1 (Bench focus)
- Barbell Bench Press: 3 x 3–5 @ RPE 6–7
- Weighted Pull-up or Lat Pulldown: 2 x 5–6 @ RPE 6–7
- Incline DB Press: 2 x 6–8 @ RPE 6
- Chest-supported Row or Seated Row: 2 x 6–8 @ RPE 6–7
- Lateral Raise: 2 x 10–12 @ RPE 6
- Triceps Pressdown: 1–2 x 10–12 @ RPE 6
- Biceps Curl: 1–2 x 10–12 @ RPE 6

Day 3: Lower 2 (Hinge focus)

- Front Squat or Hack Squat (match his accessory): 2 x 4–6 @ RPE 6–7
- Hip Thrust or Glute Bridge: 2 x 6–8 @ RPE 6
- Leg Extension: 2 x 8–10 @ RPE 6
- Hamstring Curl (seated/lying): 1–2 x 8–10 @ RPE 6
- Core: Side plank: 2 x 20–30s/side

Day 4: Upper 2 (Press/Pull balance)
- Overhead Press (barbell or DB): 3 x 3–5 @ RPE 6–7
- Barbell or Chest-Supported Row: 2 x 5–6 @ RPE 6–7
- Close-Grip Bench or Dips (match his accessory): 2 x 5–6 @ RPE 6
- Pull-down or Pull-up (alt. grip): 2 x 6–8 @ RPE 6
- Rear Delt Raise or Face Pull: 2 x 10–12 @ RPE 6
- Arm superset (optional): 1 x 10–12 each curl + triceps, easy pump

Session flow
- Warm-up: 5–7 min easy cyc/row + dynamic prep, then ramp sets for the first compound (e.g., 3–4 progressive sets of 3–5 reps to the day’s top working load, all well below effort).
- Cooldown: 5 min easy cardio + breathing; 1–2 mobility drills for the day’s prime movers.

Auto-regulation and guardrails
- Cap top RPE at 7 even if load feels light; do not chase PRs.
- Stop any set if bar speed slows meaningfully or technique deviates.
- If any joint or tendon feels irritated, drop one set and shave a rep or switch to a friendlier variation (e.g., high-bar for back squat, trap bar for deadlift, neutral-grip presses/rows).

Recovery and lifestyle for the deload week
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours/night; aim for consistent schedule.
- Steps: 7–10k/day; avoid adding extra high-intensity work.
- Nutrition:
  - Calories: at or slightly above maintenance (+0–5%), unless cutting. If in a cut, consider bringing calories up to maintenance during deload to speed recovery.
  - Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day.
  - Carbs: center around training; ~1–2 g/kg in the 3–4 hours pre/post combined.
  - Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day; add electrolytes if training in heat.
- Supplements (if already using): creatine 3–5 g/day; fish oil 1–2 g EPA/DHA; vitamin D as needed; avoid adding stimulants.
- Soft-tissue: light work only if it feels good; no aggressive scraping on sore tissues.

Example loading translation
- If his week-4 bench was 100 kg x 6 @ RPE 8.5, deload target could be 80–85 kg for 3–5 reps @ RPE 6–7.
- If his week-4 squat was 180 kg x 6 @ RPE 8.5, deload target could be 140–155 kg for 3–5 reps @ RPE 6–7.

Outcome
- Maintain technical proficiency and readiness while dissipating accumulated fatigue. He should leave every session feeling better than he started. Resume intensification block next week with normal warm-up singles or ramps to recalibrate loads.

- Extra sets added: max +1 top exposure per main lift; no accessory volume added.
- Bar speed must stay “fast.” If it slows, shut it down.
- Shoulder rule: pain ≤2/10. If shoulder talks back, revert to the original deload.

2) Primary pull (weighted pull-up or lat pulldown)

- Optional speed set: 1 x 3–4 @ RPE 6 with maximal intent on the concentric

3) Secondary chest (low-incline DB press or cable press)

4) Row (chest-supported or seated)

Deload week overview

Sessions
- 4 lifting sessions (Lower 1, Upper 1, Lower 2, Upper 2) + 1 mobility session (20 min) + 2 Zone 2 cardio sessions (30 min each).
- Bench swap: replace barbell bench with a shoulder-friendly press (neutral-grip DB or machine chest press). Overhead press remains only if pain-free; otherwise use landmine or neutral-grip DB.

Per-session set volume vs last week (Week 4 ≈ 18 working sets/session)
- Target this week: ~8–9 working sets/session (about 50–60% reduction).
- Day-by-day set maps:
  - Lower 1: from 18 → 8–9 (Back Squat 3; RDL 2; Split Squat 1–2; Leg Curl 1–2; Calf 1)
  - Upper 1: from 18 → 8–9 (Main chest press 3; Pull-up/Lat PD 2; Secondary chest 1–2; Row 1–2; Laterals 1; Triceps 0–1)
  - Lower 2: from 18 → 8–9 (Deadlift 3; Front/Hack 2; Hip Thrust 1–2; Leg Ext 1; Ham Curl 1)
  - Upper 2: from 18 → 8–9 (Main press 3; Row 2; Triceps press 1–2; Pull-up/Lat PD 1–2; Rear Delt/Face Pull 1; Arms 0–1)

Intensity vs last week
- Last week: RPE ~8.5 across compounds.
- This week: RPE 6–7 on all lifts (2–4 reps in reserve). Capped at RPE 7.5 only on the two optional “spicy” exposures midweek if you choose to include them (overwarm-up single/triple or a light cluster), with no added accessory volume.
- Load guide: ~70–75% of loads used for last week’s RPE 8.5 sets, then autoregulate to stay within RPE 6–7.
- Bar speed: all reps crisp; terminate sets if speed drops or technique degrades.

Readiness markers (optional, low-fatigue)
- 1–2 bar-speed singles at ~75–80% on squat/deadlift and shoulder-friendly press, RPE ≤7.
- Optional fixed-load submax set capped at RPE 7.

Cardio and mobility
- Zone 2 cardio: 2 sessions x 30 minutes at HR ~60–70% max (RPE 3–4), conversational.
- Mobility: 1 x 20-minute session (breath-led thoracic/shoulder/hip work), pain-free and light.

Recovery targets
- Sleep 7.5–9 hours; steps 7–10k/day.
- Nutrition: maintenance to slight surplus; protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg; carbs around training; hydrate well.

Outcome
- Total weekly lifting sets reduced ~50–60% with intensity down from RPE 8.5 → 6–7, preserving movement patterns, unloading the shoulder, and setting up the next intensification block.
